questions.question: [Memory] Compare and contrast episodic, semantic and procedural long-term memory.
questions.correctAnswer: Episodic: personal events, time-stamped, consciously recalled. Semantic: general facts, not time-stamped, consciously recalled. Procedural: skills/habits, not consciously recalled. All three are distinct LTM types with different brain regions.
questions.explanation: Episodic: personal events, time-stamped, consciously recalled. Semantic: general facts, not time-stamped, consciously recalled. Procedural: skills/habits, not consciously recalled. All three are distinct LTM types with different brain regions.

questions.question: [Animal vs Human Communication] Describe the key features that distinguish human language from animal communication systems.
questions.correctAnswer: Human language has: semanticity (meaning), generativity (infinite combinations), displacement (past/future), arbitrariness (no word-object connection), cultural transmission. Most animal communication lacks generativity and displacement - bees show some displacement but cannot create new messages.
questions.explanation: Human language has: semanticity (meaning), generativity (infinite combinations), displacement (past/future), arbitrariness (no word-object connection), cultural transmission.
